description: Light twin executive transport in the museum collection.
Regional jet airliner; forward fuselage and cabin used as a walk-through exhibit.
Ex-Australian Army 161 Recce Sqn. Sold to the museum in 2017 (ADF-Serials).
aliases: OH58; OH58A; Kiowa; CA-32; CA32; c/n 44510

description: Australian-assembled Aermacchi MB-326H. Crashed 19/08/1985 at Salt Ash, then a training aid at RSTT Wagga; on display at the museum (ADF-Serials).
aliases: CA30; MB-326H; MB326H; Macchi; c/n CA30-26

description: Two-seat Mirage IIID. Held by DSTO Adelaide to 1999, restored by ARDU in ARDU colours with a test nose cone and displayed inside the gate at RAAF Base Edinburgh; gifted to the museum in May 2018 (ADF-Serials).
aliases: Mirage IIID; MirageIII; MirageIIID; Dassault Mirage III

description: Ex-No. 38 Squadron RAAF, served with Detachment A in New Guinea from 1965. Retired to Oakey; the museum was the successful tenderer in the 2015-16 disposal (ADF-Serials).
de Havilland DH.60G Gipsy Moth. The museum records the airframe by constructor's number rather than a registration; no registration recorded here.
Served with ARDU Laverton 1957 and No. 21 Squadron; displayed at RAAF HQ North Adelaide in the 1960s and at the Mildura Warbirds Museum 1974-1980 before coming to the museum (ADF-Serials).

Royal Australian Navy Sea Venom, RAN serial N4-931, delivered 27/02/1956, flew with 724, 808 and 877 Squadrons. Formerly displayed at the Naval Aviation Museum Nowra; owned by and displayed at the museum (ADF-Serials).
Ex-RAAF and ARDU. Crash-landed at RAAF Base Edinburgh in October 1986 after a double engine failure on take-off and never flew again; sold to the museum in 1992 (ADF-Serials).

Used at Woomera for airborne photography of weapon trials including the Operation Buffalo atomic tests; struck off charge at RAAF Edinburgh 1970, at the Eureka Aviation Museum Ballarat from 1985, acquired by the museum in June 1997 and restored (ADF-Serials).
Built as the 13th production B.2 and converted to a T.4 dual-control trainer; one of the RAF-serialled Canberras that remained in Australia (ADF-Serials).
aliases: Canberra; Canberra T.4; Canberra T4; c/n 71036

description: Fokker Friendship; museum and Wikipedia lists give the fuller designation as F-27-109. Variant left blank pending a firm mark number.
Royal Australian Navy target drone delivered 16/02/1987; crashed on take-off at Jervis Bay 25/05/1992 and later held in storage by Australia's Museum of Flight, Nowra (ADF-Serials).

Engine-test and AUP prototype aircraft, retired December 2010, repainted in a SEA camouflage and white ARDU scheme and flown to Edinburgh in August 2011. Its cockpit was refurbished using the forward fuselage of FB-111A 68-0246 before transfer to the museum as the replacement for A8-134 (ADF-Serials).

Cockpit section only. Ex-RAF WK683, delivered 20/08/1952 and flown in Korea by No. 77 Squadron; named Halestorm after Sgt George Hale who shot down a MiG on 27/03/1953. Later converted to a U.21A target drone (ADF-Serials).
aliases: Meteor F.8; Meteor F8; WK683; Halestorm

description: Single-seat sailplane.
Ex-No. 10 Squadron RAAF, arrived at the museum 10/12/2017 and reassembled inside; displayed without the starboard wing because of space constraints (ADF-Serials).
aliases: AP3; AP3C; P-3; P3; P-3C; P3C; Orion; c/n 5666

description: Block 21 Hornet delivered 16/08/1988; carried flight-test instrumentation and served with No. 3 Squadron and ARDU. Transferred to Air Force History and Heritage and displayed as the ARDU jet (ADF-Serials).
aliases: F/A18; FA18; FA18A; F/A18A; F/A-18A; Hornet; c/n 560

description: Single-engine touring aircraft.

Ex-RAF EE853. Served with No. 79 Squadron RAAF coded UP-O and written off in October 1943; recovered from Kilawina Island in 1974. Owned by Langdon Badger of Adelaide and displayed as A58-146 UP-O at the museum since 1998 (ADF-Serials).
aliases: EE853; Spitfire Vc; Spitfire Mk Vc

description: Homebuilt single-engine aircraft flown by Jon Johanson on record-setting long-distance flights.

Royal Australian Navy anti-submarine helicopter, first flight 06/08/1963, served aboard HMAS Melbourne and HMAS Stalwart. Instructional airframe from 1987, at the Fleet Air Arm Museum from 1991 and at the museum since 2000 (ADF-Serials).
Long-term restoration project; the museum records the airframe as EF954/AW965.
Long-term restoration project; wings under restoration as of 2025-26 per the museum's own website.
Sounding rocket displayed with a Lupus 1A booster as part of the Woomera heritage rocket collection held for the Defence Science and Technology Group.
High-altitude sounding rocket from the Woomera heritage rocket collection.
High Altitude Density research rocket displayed with a Gosling booster motor; Woomera heritage rocket collection. Known as the HAD sounding rocket.
Jabiru hypersonic research vehicle from the Woomera programme.
